scope: Screen additional open-source DXF parser/render and geometry-consumer routes beyond the existing comparator set; distinguish entity recognition, semantic parser, renderer, graph retention, and kernel conversion evidence.

method.kind: Public repository source, package manifest, documentation, and issue review
method.evidenceBoundary: Source and documentation observations only. No peer parser output, rendered geometry, BRL-CAD import, malformed-input reproduction, or local implementation behavior was executed. Mutable branch source is not a release/artifact identity.

evidence.observed: dxf-parser is MIT-licensed, documents a string input API, mostly 2D support, and explicitly lists 3DSOLID as unsupported. Its current DxfParser source registers explicit handlers including 3DFACE and POLYLINE. three-dxf documents that it renders objects produced by DxfParser and also lists 3DSOLID as unsupported. The viewer and parser therefore share parser lineage.
doesNotEstablish: full OBJECTS/owner graph or opaque-record preservation
a second independent parser vote from three-dxf
evidence.planUse: Optional one-time ASCII projection comparator for overlapping explicit entities only, after pinning exact package artifacts. Do not add a dependency, per-slice check, or 3D-solid support claim.

evidence.observed: The package manifest says version 0.3.2 and MIT. The project README lists 3DSOLID and OBJECTS. The entity dispatcher instantiates and routes a Solid3D parser, but this source review did not inspect or execute its payload semantics. ObjectsParser.parse() advances through the OBJECTS section without storing records, and Parser.parse()'s returned object includes HEADER, CLASSES, TABLES, BLOCKS, and ENTITIES, but not OBJECTS. The API is text-string based; binary DXF behavior was not established.
doesNotEstablish: ACIS payload decoding or semantic solid validity from a Solid3D dispatch entry
OBJECTS identity/owner/reference retention in the returned document
binary DXF support or a released artifact's exact runtime behavior
evidence.planUse: Keep as a source-inspection lead only. Before any graph or solid comparator use, pin an artifact and prove the returned model retains a generated OBJECTS record/edge and that a 3DSOLID payload is semantically interpreted rather than merely recognized. No installation/run is presently justified.

evidence.topic: BRL-CAD dxf-g conversion and hostile POLYFACE issue
evidence.observed: BRL-CAD documents DXF import through dxf-g and faceted DXF output through g-dxf; this is a geometry-conversion route rather than general document round-trip. Open issue #228 reports an AddressSanitizer heap over-read in the normal dxf-g import path when untrusted POLYFACE indices address beyond the vertex pool. This report was not independently reproduced in this review.
doesNotEstablish: a libdxfrw vulnerability or valid-file semantic disagreement
current behavior of an exact pinned/fixed BRL-CAD build
DXF owner graph, opaque records, ACIS/B-rep semantics, or DWG support
safe eligibility for malformed-input differential testing
evidence.planUse: Do not send malformed controls to dxf-g while the safety report remains unresolved. A future pinned fixed build may be used for positive locally authored explicit-facet projection only, with exact version, warnings, units, topology, and output disposition.

optionalComparatorRules: At most one JavaScript parser/viewer route in a single composed checkpoint; three-dxf does not add parser independence over dxf-parser.
Keep JavaScript comparator scope to ASCII explicit-entity projection and compare against a separately authored raw-tag manifest.
Do not admit @dxfjs/parser for OBJECTS graph evidence until returned-model retention is demonstrated; do not infer ACIS semantics from entity dispatch.
Require a pinned BRL-CAD revision cleared of the reported importer safety issue before any malformed-input use; no malformed peer execution is authorized by this plan.
